text_en: Tel Aviv central bus station: Two Palestinian suicide bombers attack a neighborhood in Tel Aviv, killing at least 23 people and injuring 103.
The discovery of OGLE-TR-56b, the first exoplanet to be discovered through transit photometry, is announced.
North Korea announces its withdrawal from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.
The last signal from NASA's Pioneer 10 spacecraft is received, some 12.2 billion kilometers (7.6 billion mi) from Earth.
Waterfall rail accident: An Intercity Tangara G set train derails near Waterfall, killing 7 and injuring 40 others. The cause was of a faulty deadman's brake.
At the conclusion of the STS-107 mission, the Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates during reentry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts on board.

The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is renamed to "Serbia and Montenegro" (after its two constituent states) after its leaders reconstitute the country into a loose state-union between Montenegro and Serbia, marking an end to the 73-year-long use of the name "Yugoslavia" by a sovereign state.

U.S. Secretary of State Colin Powell gives a speech to the United Nations presenting the case for a military invasion of Iraq. It will later be discovered that the United States Bush administration misled him when preparing his testimony.
North Korea announces that it has resumed its nuclear weapons program.: 81
The 2003 Cricket World Cup begins. It is held in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Kenya, and it ends on March 23 with Australia defeating India in the final.
The first set of data from the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe is published.
Dolly the sheep, the clone of a mammal, dies.: 479
Millions of people worldwide take part in massive anti-war protests in anticipation of the United States and its allies invading Iraq to overthrow Saddam Hussein's regime.
The Station nightclub fire: A fire broke out at a music venue in West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States, killing 100 people and injuring 230.
2003 Bachu earthquake: A 6.8 Mwearthquake strikes in Xinjiang, killing 257 people.
The War in Darfur begins after rebel groups rise up against the Sudanese government.
Khalid Sheikh Mohammed of al-Qaeda is captured in Rawalpindi, Pakistan.
SCO Group files a lawsuit against IBM as part of an ongoing dispute regarding the use of Unix in the development of Linux.
Peace talks break down in the First Ivorian Civil War.: 115–116
Malta approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Former General François Bozizé seizes power through a military coup in the Central African Republic.
U.S. President George W. Bush presents a 48-hour ultimatum for Iraqi president Saddam Hussein to resign.
The Iraq War begins with the invasion of Iraq by the United States and allied forces.
In its first military operation, the European Union takes over peacekeeping operations in Macedonia from NATO's Operation Allied Harmony.: 251
The Archaeological Survey of India orders that Hindus be allowed to worship in the Kamal Maula Mosque.
U.S. forces seize control of Baghdad, ending the rule of Saddam Hussein.
Hungary approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Five college students are murdered in an unsolved arson in Columbus, Ohio.
The Human Genome Project is completed, with 99% of the human genome sequenced to 99.99% accuracy.

The Treaty of Accession is signed in Athens between the European Union and ten countries (Czech Republic, Estonia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Malta, Poland, Slovenia and Slovakia), concerning these countries' accession into the EU, leading to the 2004 enlargement of the European Union.
Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee visits Kashmir and expresses support for peace negotiations with Pakistan.: 95
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam break away from peace talks in the Sri Lankan Civil War.: 107
The iTunes Store launches.: 87
A ceasefire takes effect in the First Ivorian Civil War.: 115–116
John Paul II visits Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, becoming the first pope ever to enter a mosque.: 471
2003 Znamenskoye suicide bombing: Chechen suicide bombers attack a government office in Znamenskoye, Russia, killing at least 59 people.
Contact with infected prairie dogs causes the first outbreak of human mpox in the Western Hemisphere. Cases continue until June 11.: 202
Slovakia approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Peace talks break down in the insurgency in Aceh and the Indonesian government launches new attacks against the insurgents.
The Eurovision Song Contest 2003 takes place in Riga, Latvia, and is won by Turkish entrant Sertab Erener with the song "Everyway That I Can".
A Boeing 727 aircraft is stolen from an airport in Luanda, Angola triggering an international terrorist investigation by the FBI and CIA. The aircraft and its pilots were never found.
Georges Rutaganda becomes the first person to be convicted of war crimes by the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, and his previous charges are upheld.
Prometea, the world's first cloned horse, is born.
The Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty comes into effect between Russia and the United States.
Mars Express launches, containing the Beagle 2 lander.
An agreement is reached for the United Nations to form a Khmer Rouge Tribunal.
Poland approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
NASA launches the Spirit rover.: 477
The Czech Republic approves joining the European Union in a referendum.
Former President of France Valéry Giscard d'Estaing presents his draft for a Constitution of the European Union.
Warring parties in the Democratic Republic of the Congo sign a peace accord, bringing an end to the Second Congo War.
SARS is declared to be contained by the World Health Organization.
NASA launches the Opportunity rover.: 477
The Iraqi Governing Council is created by the United States as an ethnically diverse provisional government of Iraq.
The United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia agrees to disband.: 102
Major Fernando Pereira leads a failed coup against President Fradique de Menezes in São Tomé and Príncipe.
The Regional Assistance Mission to the Solomon Islands, led by Australia, begins after ethnic violence engulfs the island country.
The Tasman Spirit oil spill occurs in Pakistan.: 195
The final Volkswagen Beetle is produced.
Milomir Stakić receives the first life sentence issued by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.
The discovery of the dinosaur species Rajasaurus narmadensis is announced.

An overloaded power grid following the failure of FirstEnergy's alarm system in their control room causes the Northeast blackout of 2003, affecting more than 50 million people in the United States and Canada with nearly 100 related deaths.
Libya formally accepts civil responsibility for the bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 in 1988.
Element 110 is formally named darmstadtium by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry.
Peace talks between Maoist rebels and the Nepalese government are interrupted by resumed hostilities in the Nepalese Civil War.
A peace agreement is reached to formally end the Second Liberian Civil War.: 118
The G21 (later called the G20 developing nations) forms in response to disputes around the upcoming World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2003.
The Brazilian VLS-1 launcher explodes on the launchpad on August 22, killing 21 people.: 276
Imam Ali mosque bombing: A bomb kills at least 125 people, including Mohammad Baqir al-Hakim, at a Shia mosque in Najaf, Iraq.
Typhoon Dujuan makes landfall in Guangdong as a category 1 typhoon with sustained winds of 90 mph.
Hurricane Fabian strikes Bermuda.
Armenia abolishes capital punishment entirely, following a law on August 1 that abolished it in most cases.
Typhoon Maemi, makes landfall in South Korea as a category 3 typhoon with sustained winds of 125 mph.
Hurricane Isabel makes landfall in North Carolina.
The United Nations establishes the United Nations Mission in Liberia with Resolution 1509.
Latvia approves joining the European Union in a referendum.

October 12 – The 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup is held in the United States after the tournament is moved from China due to the SARS outbreak. Germany win their first title after they defeated Sweden in the final with a golden goal.
NASA ends the Galileo probe mission after nearly 14 years by sending it into Jupiter's atmosphere.
The Hubble Space Telescope starts the Hubble Ultra-Deep Field, making 800 exposures, until January 16, 2004.
Two parties in the Second Sudanese Civil War, the National Islamic Front and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement, reach a peace agreement.: 119
The 8.3 Mw Tokachi earthquake occurs off the coast of Hokkaido.
SMART-1, an ESA spaceprobe and ESA's first mission to the moon, is launched from Kourou, French Guiana.
Maxim restaurant suicide bombing: A Palestinian suicide bomber attacks a restaurant in Haifa, Israel, killing at least 19 people.
Israeli warplanes strike alleged Islamic jihad bases inside Syrian territory, the first Israeli attack on the country since the 1973 Yom Kippur War.
Hezbollah and the Israel Defense Forces engage in hostilities in the Shebaa Farms.
Nokia releases a handheld game console, the N-Gage. It becomes a major critical failure in the gaming industry.
November 22 – The 2003 Rugby World Cup is held in Australia and is won by England who defeated Australia in the final after extra time.
Gyude Bryant becomes President of Liberia as a compromise choice after former President Charles Taylor fled the country during the Second Liberian Civil War.: 80
China launches Shenzhou 5, the country's first human spaceflight.
Mother Teresa is beatified by Pope John Paul II.
After acknowledging that it has produced enriched uranium, Iran agrees to suspend its nuclear program.
Concorde makes its last commercial flight, bringing the era of airliner supersonic travel to an end.
The United Nations Security Council adopts Resolution 1511 to approve American-led governance in Iraq.: 346
The International Court of Justice rules in the Oil Platforms case that the United States was not justified in its 1987 attacks on Iranian oil platforms but that neither party violated a 1955 treaty.
The dwarf planet Sedna is discovered by a team of astronomers led by Michael E. Brown from the Palomar Observatory.

Suicide bombings occur in Istanbul. Further attacks occur five days later. They kill 63 people between them, making them the two deadliest terror attacks in Turkey, and cause uncertainty in the international economy.: 177

Baghdad DHL attempted shootdown incident: Shortly after takeoff, a DHL Express cargo plane is struck on the left wing by a surface-to-air missile fired by the Islamic Army in Iraq and forced to land. All three crew members survive without injuries.
A ceasefire is reached at the Line of Control in Kashmir.: 95
The supersonic passenger jet, Concorde, makes its last ever flight from Heathrow Airport in London to Bristol Filton Airport.
Trial of Stanislav Galić: The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia sentences Stanislav Galić to 20 years in prison for crimes against humanity.
The United Nations Convention Against Corruption is opened for signing.: 493
Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, is captured in the small town of Ad-Dawr by the U.S. Army.
The 6.6 Mw Bam earthquake occurs in Iran.
The Protocol on Heavy Metals comes into effect.: 493
